ranked.headline: Spatial priors guide integration and reconstruction of spatial transcriptomics data
ranked.summary: Recent published and preprint work extends spatial transcriptomics models toward multi-omics alignment, reference transfer, and foundation model integration.

ranked.headline: Representation fusion and pretrained adaptation for biomolecular prediction
ranked.summary: Recent work tests whether fused graph, sequence, and text representations, and adapted foundation models, improve drug and perturbation prediction.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein representations drive diverse residue-level binding site predictors
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and journal papers pair protein language models and structure encoders with graph and state-space architectures for binding site detection.

ranked.headline: Models integrating incomplete and small-sample multi-omics data for prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and published work add missingness-aware, uncertainty-aware and pathway-constrained architectures for heterogeneous omics layers.

ranked.headline: Deep learning infers cell state from images and omics beyond direct measurement
ranked.summary: Deep models now infer molecular state from spatial, label-free, and single-cell imaging and omics data at finer resolution than direct measurement.

ranked.headline: Machine learning ranks non-coding and rare-disease variants by predicted impact
ranked.summary: Multi-species sequence models and phenotype-aware ranking extend variant prioritization to non-coding and rare-disease settings.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking and generative models for TCR and antibody antigen recognition
ranked.summary: Strict evaluation conditions, negative data quality, and confidence metrics now shape how TCR and antibody binding tools are judged.

ranked.headline: Read-level data increasingly drive variant, copy number, and mosaicism inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications derive somatic, copy number, methylation, and reliability inferences directly from sequencing read data.

ranked.headline: Protein language models drive sequence-only stability and mutation effect prediction
ranked.summary: Sequence-only protein language models now outperform structure-informed predictors for ΔTm in controlled ablations.

ranked.headline: New pipelines, atlases and databases for benchmarked genomic and single-cell analysis
ranked.summary: Recent releases pair large harmonized resources with explicit benchmarking of analysis methods across omics modalities.

ranked.headline: Structured dependency inference from single-cell and spatial omics under external priors
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics data now support network inference that couples priors, latent activity and trajectory context.

ranked.headline: Read-level evidence defining transcript ends and RNA cleavage sites
ranked.summary: Recent tools model read classes, soft-clipped reads and direct RNA evidence to define transcript boundaries and processing sites more precisely.

ranked.headline: Statistical models infer cell states and phenotypes from bulk and single-cell omics
ranked.summary: Deconvolution, co-expression, and foundation-model approaches now convert bulk and single-cell measurements into phenotypic and clinical inference.

ranked.headline: Segmental duplication and convergent adaptation across vertebrates, flies and spiders
ranked.summary: Long-read genomes now resolve duplication landscapes and convergent selection across vertebrates, Drosophila, mealybugs and spiders.

ranked.headline: Population-scale variant inference from short- and long-read sequencing data
ranked.summary: Pangenome, k-mer, and long-read methods now resolve rare, structural, and repetitive variation across cohorts of thousands of individuals.

ranked.headline: Learned and physics-based models quantify peptide and small-molecule ligand binding
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs FEP+ validation on macrocyclic peptides with learned models for peptide design, screening, and permeability.

ranked.headline: Spatial structure in epidemic reproduction and mobility-informed transmission prediction
ranked.summary: Mobile-phone mobility and contact-matrix reproduction ratios are being tested for predicting spatial epidemic spread.

ranked.headline: Deep learning refines long-read variant, splice, and RNA modification inference
ranked.summary: Learned models now address error correction, filtering, and evaluation across long-read and transcriptome sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic and trajectory models couple single-cell immune data with cell-state dynamics
ranked.summary: Single-cell immune data are now coupled to dynamic, clonotype, and agent-based models to predict fate and treatment response.

ranked.headline: Effective models reduce birth-death, epidemic, and replicator population dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints derive effective descriptions of T-cell clone fixation, recurrent epidemics, alternating-environment persistence, and replicator evolution.

ranked.headline: Learned representations predict protein flexibility, enzyme function, natural products
ranked.summary: Representation models are now evaluated on unseen enzyme classes and discovery-relevant tasks, not only in-distribution accuracy.

ranked.headline: Simulation probes nanobody fluctuations and membrane-lytic peptide activity
ranked.summary: Multiscale and MD-informed models now address S-layer nanobody inhibition and membrane-contact prediction for antimicrobial peptides.

ranked.headline: Learned and physics-based models of protein structure, stability, and druggable sites
ranked.summary: Open co-folding, distance-conditioned prediction, and MD-based pocket mapping are extending structure-based protein modeling as of July 2026.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked validation of computational stages in microbiome and microbial genomics tools
ranked.summary: Recent items pair new tools with explicit benchmarks of their outputs, spanning batch correction, CRISPR spacer matching, and capture simulation.

ranked.headline: Sequence models and replicate-aware methods refine epigenomic regulatory inference
ranked.summary: Recent methods link methylation, chromatin structure and sequence models to regulatory function while controlling replicate-level false positives.

ranked.headline: Tools infer microbial interactions and functions from genomic data
ranked.summary: Recent methods predict microbial relations and functional traits at strain resolution, drawing on pangenomes, phylogenies, and knowledge graphs.

ranked.headline: Language models and literature retrieval attach functional context to genes and proteins
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply retrieval-augmented language models and literature mining to gene and protein annotation and enrichment analysis.

ranked.headline: Structural descriptors link protein architecture to phenotype, disorder, and stability
ranked.summary: Purpose-built structural descriptors now quantify packing, disorder localization, and variant phenotypes across genome-wide and protein-family scales.

ranked.headline: Spatial profiling links cell size, senescence and cell states to tissue context
ranked.summary: Spatial readouts now reach intact tissue and network-embedded domains, enabling quantitative analysis of cell state, size and organization in situ.

ranked.headline: Inference-based and validated models are linking neural measurements to function
ranked.summary: Neural measurements are increasingly fitted to biophysical, encoding, and behavioral models with reusable open software rather than descriptive mapping alone.

ranked.headline: Unbalanced transport models infer cell-state dynamics from unpaired single-cell data
ranked.summary: Cross-sectional and unpaired single-cell and methylation data now support trajectory and population-mass modeling without time-resolved sampling.

ranked.headline: Compressed k-mer and BWT indexes enable direct querying of pangenome-scale sequence
ranked.summary: New compressed k-mer and BWT-based indexes lower space costs while keeping direct queries on pangenome-scale sequence data.

ranked.headline: Gene flow undermines phylogenetic topology inference from conserved genomic loci
ranked.summary: Gene flow can mislead species-tree and introgression inference, motivating outgroup-free methods and quantitative measures of asymmetric virus-host dependence.

ranked.headline: E. coli growth serves as a living reservoir computer for classification and sensing
ranked.summary: Living bacterial growth is being framed as computation, alongside data-driven models linking microbial genotype and sequence to function.

ranked.headline: Spatial snapshots and mechanistic models: when do dynamics become identifiable?
ranked.summary: Spatial measurements are now analyzed with dynamical models, making identifiability and well-posedness central to interpreting inferred mechanisms.

ranked.headline: Simulations link glycan modifications to receptor binding and protein assembly
ranked.summary: Molecular dynamics, free energy calculations, and structure prediction now address glycan-dependent binding, glycoprotein assembly, and immune recognition.

ranked.headline: Summary-statistic methods map heritability, causal genes and regulatory targets
ranked.summary: Recent methods extract heritability, causal gene and regulatory-target inferences from GWAS summary statistics and multi-omics resources.

ranked.headline: Models predict NMD sensitivity and calibrate RNA-seq splicing estimates
ranked.summary: Paired genomic and transcriptomic data now allow variant-level NMD prediction, while splicing metrics require explicit correction for NMD-targeted transcripts.

ranked.headline: Software for simulating, visualizing and benchmarking ancestral recombination graphs
ranked.summary: New tools now pair spatiotemporal ARG simulation and GPU-accelerated biobank-scale visualization with pangenome benchmarking from coalescent genealogies.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models annotate lipids, peptides, and metabolites from tandem MS data
ranked.summary: Transformer and foundation-model embeddings now sit inside LC-MS and proteomics search workflows, shifting annotation beyond conventional database matching.
